newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Foncier unions push mediator for break-up halt.
newsitem.headline: Cr Foncier unions push mediator for break-up halt.

text.p: Unions at Credit Foncier will press government appointed mediator Philippe Rouvillois at a 1430 GMT meeting for a clear declaration that the planned break-up of their troubled group is being put on hold, a union member said on Thursday.
The union leader told Reuters the meeting, on the seventh day of a staff occupation of the Paris headquarters, had been agreed with Rouvillois.
"We're looking for a strong signal from the state, at the moment it appears the (break-up) plan has been frozen," the union member said.
Earlier, government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said draft legislation concerning a break-up of the home loans bank was being "kept in waiting".
This comment was taken by unions at Credit Foncier, who met on Thursday morning, as meaning the break-up would be put on hold but the unions would seek a clearer statement, the union member said.

The cross-union grouping at Credit Foncier was also due to meet its counterpart from the savings bank grouping Caisses d'Epargne and a union grouping from the semi-state sector later in the day, the union member said, asking not to be identified.

The government has been planning to allow cooperatively run Credit Immobilier take over the home loans portfolio of Credit Foncier and pass legislation to set up a state holding company which would take over and wind down the rest of the group.
"The French people rose up against giving part of Thomson to Daewoo for one symbolic franc. In our case it's not even for a symbolic franc, it's for nothing," said the union member.
"It's a free gift the government is offering," to Credit Immobilier," the unionist said.
"We want to see Credit Immobilier play the role of a real takeover, which means paying for what it takes, or else that it takes a stake in our capital like any other partner would do."
"We can look at another scheme with the SACI (Credit Immobilier)," the union member said.

The government recently suspended the privatisation of state-owned defence and consumer electronics group Thomson SA via a sale for a symbolic franc to Lagardere, amid objections from staff, and crucially, France's privatisation commission.
Lagardere had planned to sell on Thomson SA's consumer electronics arm, Thomson Multimedia, to South Korea's Daewoo Electronics for a symbolic franc as well.
